guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Without direction, reparenting can become permissive. The child receives attention but doesn’t develop. Candy, screens, and escape from anything difficult can masquerade as self-love.
brief:
- the meaning, in plain words: without the Guide's direction, looking after your little one can slide into spoiling it. Sweets and screens, and getting it out of anything hard, can all pass for loving yourself.
- one everyday moment a reader would recognize from their own life, told in a sentence or two, the way the author's own paragraphs do it: "Your dog can chew up your good shoes and be forgiven before you've found the other one." or "you might be like the firefighters who become arsonists to keep themselves employed." Never a moment from the author's own life: the reader's, or anybody's.
- context, not for the text: P1, right before this, says the Guide asks hard things of your little one, at its own pace. The article already says a break when your little one has had enough is fine ("Okay, that's enough for today," and try something gentler), so the trap is dodging anything hard for good, not a pause. Don't say the child stops growing: P1 and The Chicken-and-Egg Problem already say it.
- context, not for the text: the last drafts of this paragraph read AI. Each re-said the guide's sentences in the guide's order: a thesis sentence first, a "so" chain, a list of three, a closing lesson, every sentence a general "can" or "may" claim. Use your own order and your own words; keep a hedge only where the meaning needs one.
- context, not for the text: don't use these words from the guide unless nothing else fits: masquerade, permissive, direction.
